title: A global coffee-shop chain: external factors case and 12-mark frame
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 32 (Pupil PDF worksheet: external factors case and 12-mark frame)
intro: Lesson 32. Read the case, then evaluate the statement.

passage.title: Kahwa House plc
paras: Kahwa House plc runs 2,400 coffee shops in 18 countries. It buys its coffee beans in US dollars and reports its profits in pounds.

Over the last year the pound has weakened from £1 = $1.40 to £1 = $1.20, so its beans cost more. Several countries have passed laws banning single-use cups, and customers are asking where its coffee comes from and whether farmers are paid fairly.
At the same time, a customer survey found that service in its shops has become slower, and a new menu launched last spring sold badly. Two rival chains are opening shops next to its busiest branches.
passage.source: All businesses, people and figures in this case are fictional, made up for practice.

blocks.h: Answer frame (12 marks: both sides, then a supported judgement)

blocks.text: 'External factors are the main threat to Kahwa House's success.' Evaluate this statement. (12 marks)

frame.label: For: point and chain of reasoning in context
Against: point and chain of reasoning in context
Judgement
frame.prompt: Decide, give the main reason, and say what it depends on.

markScheme.a: External: a weaker pound raised bean costs from £400m to £470m; cup laws add costs; pressure on ethical sourcing (CSR). Internal: satisfaction fell from 82% to 71%, slower service and a failed menu are within its control and explain lost customers. Judgement: e.g. internal factors matter more because profit fell by £70m while revenue still rose, so it depends on whether management can fix service. Level 4 (10-12): developed chains of reasoning on both sides in context, and a supported judgement with 'it depends on'. Level 3 (7-9): both sides developed, judgement partly supported. Level 2 (4-6): some development, one-sided or generic. Level 1 (1-3): points identified.
